handback.t:
W16 (MAX-VECTORS) is finished: all six items were measured, and results/g15_board_entry.md has one "### VERIFY REQUEST — W16 — ..." block per item. It carries rerun commands, numbers with spread, and a "Not done" list. Latencies came from a box at ~100 % CPU (other workers), so trust ratios, recall and bytes/vector; absolute latency is ±50–100 %.

I edited nothing in src/*.rs. I added src/bin/g15_vectors.rs and src/bin/g15_common/ and used my own target dir C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r6 with 2 rayon threads. Results are in results/g15_*; the first, heavily loaded runs of quant/scale/conc/flat are in results/g15_run1/. Patch proposals are in results/g15_proposed_patch.md.

How it was measured: single-query latency on one thread, 3 timed passes per config, recall@10 against exact f32 brute force. Bytes/vector come from a counting allocator. Each JSON also stores a fixed-scan load probe, which ran 1.4–2.7 ms normally and 4.3–5.8 ms in the loaded runs.

Data: synthetic hierarchical clusters (dim 384), plus real MiniLM-384 and BGE-768 from results/g1_emb_[A-D]_*.f32. After dropping exact duplicates the real sets have only 23,453 unique rows (23,153 base rows for MiniLM). Both real corpora are synthetic templated text, and MiniLM queries are held-out base rows because no MiniLM query embeddings are stored. f6_minilm_fixture.json and f8_bge_embeddings.f32 (2,424 vectors each) were too small to use.

**Best configs, hnsw_rs (3 rebuilds each, N≈23–30k, dim 384/768, single thread)**
- recall@10 ≥ 0.95: M32/efc100/ef10 on the 384-d sets and M16/efc100/ef10 on BGE-768. p50 is about 0.08–0.13 ms, p99 about 0.2–0.4 ms.
- recall@10 ≥ 0.99: M48/efc200/ef16 on all three sets (M32/efc100/ef24 on synthetic, 0.990). p50 is about 0.13–0.25 ms, p99 about 0.23–0.5 ms. Bytes/vector are 6.8–8.7 KB.
- ef below k is clamped to k, so ef=10 is the floor, and the frontier sits at that floor. Higher ef buys at most 0.005 recall for 2–10x p99.
- M matters more than efc, and efc 100 is enough up to recall ~0.98.
- An AVX2+FMA distance kernel (runtime-dispatched, no build flags) cuts p50 by 9–17 % and p99 by 7–43 %, with recall unchanged.

**Max vectors per GB (index only; recall = mini23k / synth 1e5 / synth 1e6)**

| Config | B/vec | M vec/GB | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|
| turbovec 2-bit | 100 | 10.0 | 0.92 / 0.56 / 0.36 |
| turbovec 3-bit | 148 | 6.8 | 0.96 / 0.73 / n/a |
| turbovec 4-bit | 196 | 5.1 | 0.98 / 0.85 / 0.77 |
| int8 flat | 388 | 2.6 | 0.997 / 0.976 / 0.963 |
| block-fp16 flat | 816 | 1.2 | 1.000 |
| flat f32 | 1536 | 0.65 | 1.000 |
| HNSW M16 | 6.2–6.5 KB | 0.16 | — |

- turbovec with 4x f32 rerank reaches 0.999–1.000 up to 1e6, but only if the f32 copy is on SSD or mmap. Kept in RAM it costs ~1.7 KB/vec, no saving over flat f32. The SSD cost was not measured.
- Block-fp16 (shared exponent per 32 values, i16 mantissa) loses no recall (0 of 3,000 top-10 slots differ on all three sets) at 53 % of f32 bytes, with a scan about 19–26 % faster. f16 and bf16 are slightly lossier; int8 loses 0.003–0.037 depending on the set.
- My PQ-lite is a negative result: recall 0.31–0.89 without rerank, strictly worse than turbovec 2-bit, with a much slower build and scan.

**Scaling at N = 1e4 / 1e5 / 3e5 / 1e6**
- Peak process working set was 1.86 GB at 1e6. The 1e6 run went ahead because 5.3 GB of RAM was free at start.
- HNSW was skipped at 1e6. It measured 6.2 KB/vec at 1e5/3e5, so the projected total is about 7.7 GB, over the 3 GB cap.
- At 1e5, HNSW M16/efc200 builds in 56.5 s quiet vs 116.5 s loaded, with recall 0.978–0.990 at p50 0.43–0.75 ms.
- At 3e5 (one build only, 188 s), HNSW recall collapses to 0.84–0.92 at ef 64–256. M32/M48 were not tried at that size.
- At 1e6, turbovec 4-bit + 4x rerank gives recall 0.999 at p99 12.2 ms on 1 thread and 8.2 ms on 2 threads. Flat f32 is 64.6 ms p99; int8 is 17.8 ms p99 at recall 0.963.
- Synthetic noise-heavy data makes recall at large N pessimistic for approximate methods. I found no real fixture ≥ 1e5 to check against.

**Concurrency (N = 1e5, shared index)**
- HNSW read-only scales 4.2x from 1 to 4 readers (1,122 to 4,673 qps), with no lock needed. One insert thread running flat out (~700 inserts/s) does not measurably hurt readers.
- turbovec behind an RwLock scales 4.1x for readers, but a writer adding 64 vectors every 50 ms gives p99 of 18 ms and about 28 % less throughput. Every add invalidates its cache.
- Flat scan scales only 2.4x, limited by memory bandwidth.

**Flat vs HNSW crossover (dim 384, recall ≥ 0.95, two runs)**
- Flat wins up to about N=5k and HNSW wins from about 10k. At 30k HNSW is 8–9x faster.
- int8 scan with rerank (recall 1.000) ties HNSW at 10k.
- This does not reproduce the earlier "flat fastest at 30k"; I could not find why.

**Side finding on turbovec memory:** turbovec 1.0 keeps about chunk_rows × dim × 4 bytes of scratch alive after adding in several batches (77–96 MB for 50k-row chunks at dim 384, none for a single add). Patch P4 proposes capping add batches at 2,048 rows.

Proposed patches (none applied):
- **P1:** AVX2+FMA runtime-dispatched dot in memory.rs.
- **P2:** HNSW defaults to M32/efc100/ef24, or M48/efc200/ef16 for ≥ 0.99.
- **P3:** automatic flat-to-HNSW switch at about 8k.
- **P4:** cap turbovec add batches at 2,048 rows.
- **P5:** an int8 flat backend.

**Not done:**
- HNSW at 1e6.
- Any real corpus ≥ 1e5.
- SSD rerank, persistence, deletes and filtered search.
- Only one HNSW build at 3e5 and one quantiser build at 1e6.
- The HNSW sweep frontier uses one build per config; the confirm blocks are the 3-rebuild figures.
